description: Issue #839 AC1: `define foo` twice is an ERROR, not a silent override. Phase-1 registration raises `ol-duplicate-definition` carrying BOTH spans — `source_span` at the later declaration, `params.original_span` at the earlier one (`spec/error-model.md:126,144-147`) — and `spec/execution-model.md:86-88` makes it "MUST NOT be a silent override". The two bodies print DIFFERENT values on purpose, so the fixture discriminates between all three candidate rules — last-wins prints `222`, first-wins prints `111`, and only the ruling's rule produces the empty event stream asserted here. The `foo` call on line 7 is likewise deliberate: it proves nothing runs at all, rather than merely that the definitions were rejected. Core Language only, because phase-1 registration is unconditional — no profile decides whether a program may declare a name. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why only one report survives and it reads `stage: "semantic"`.
